parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Section three. You are here with two students called Ruth and Edward discussing their assignment about a conservation issue involving elephants in Kenya. First, you have some time to look at the questions twenty-one to twenty-four.

Now, listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.

Right, Edward. I've got some notes here for our conservation assignment. I had a look at the research you mentioned in Kenya. I hadn't realized that farmers were having so many problems with elephants eating their crops there.

Yes. The trouble is when elephants get into farmers' field and destroy their crops, that has all sorts of other results.

I don't suppose the farmers can just get up and go somewhere else?

No, but it's a real problem because farmers are shooting the elephants to keep their crops safe, and then the other elephants are affected and become very hostile to humans. But you can see for the farmers, it's not homes and families that have been threatened.

And it's understandable that farmers don't feel like supporting elephant conservation if their own livelihood is being destroyed. You feel you have the right to defend your property.

Exactly. So I thought for our assignment, we can start with the problem, then introduce the solutions they've been experimenting with.

So now we get onto the bees. I never thought elephants would be afraid of bees. But I suppose even if you're as big as an elephant, a bee sting can still hurt.

Well, I think it depends. Bees can't sting through the thick skin on an adult elephant's body, but they target the sensitive areas, like near the eyes.

Oh, that must really hurt. And I heard they get right inside the elephant's trunk and sting there.

Yes. And then there are the baby elephants, the calves, which have thinner skin, so they can be really badly affected, especially if they get attacked by a whole swarm of bees.

So elephants with babies may be threatened by bees even if they don't get stung themselves.

Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to read questions twenty-five to thirty.

Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.

Okay, so next week we can go on to describe the experiments based on this fear that elephants have of bees. So there was one way. They hung containers full of bees in trees near the farms.

And they listened in trees without containers?

And they found the elephants trampled down the trees that didn't have any containers.

And stayed well away from the ones with the bees in. Okay. So did you read the articles about the experiment where it was done with the audio recording of bees instead of real bees?

No.

Well, they've got a recording of a swarm of angry bees, and they played it to herds of elephants out in the wild, and they all stopped what they were doing immediately and stood erect with their heads up and their ears extended.

They must have been really aware there was danger somewhere.

But not the sort of danger that they can face up to and charge. So they dashed off in the opposite direction. They kept turning their heads around.

Presumably looking for the swarm of bees, which wasn't there.

Yes. And researchers tested eighteen different herds of the elephants, and all but one responded in a same way.

Maybe that herd just didn't hear it properly. It seems a very small exception to the main finding.

I think researchers actually concluded that this particular herd lacked any experience of bees. They've never encountered any, so they weren't afraid of the recording.

Right. Oh, so that was the reason.

Exactly. But what surprised the researchers was from the seventeen herds they did take action when they heard the recording, they found almost fifty percent of the herds did this very quickly, within ten seconds of hearing the recording.

Ah, that's interesting.

Right. So playing the recordings of bees could be a good deterrent to elephants, but it's not all that straightforward, actually.

Yes. You've got to have the electricity to run the machinery.

No, that's okay. It can run on batteries. But the whole thing's quite difficult for electrical outlet, which might be easy, and then someone's got to set it all out and make sure it's working. That's not difficult, but it's really a job.

They're trying other methods as well, like electric fences to keep the elephants away from the crops. They haven't had much success. But when they hang cowbells on the fences, that seemed to scare them off.

Yes. I've read they tried chili peppers as a deterrent too, but that didn't scare the elephants at all.

Right. So I think we've got plenty of information.

That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

questions.question: What TWO impacts could be made by bees to elephants?

analyses.content: 录音中直接说明，蜜蜂会专门瞄准大象眼睛附近这种“敏感区域（sensitive areas）”去攻击，直接锁定了选项B。
听到“厚皮肤（thick skin）”你可能就想选A，但录音里明确表示了蜜蜂根本“刺不透（can't sting through）”，所以A是完全相反的干扰项。
Well, I think it depends. Bees can't sting through the thick skin on an adult elephant's body, but they target the sensitive areas, like near the eyes.

questions.question: What TWO impacts could be made by bees to elephants?

analyses.content: 录音强调，小象因为皮比较薄，一旦遭到蜜蜂攻击会受到“非常严重的影响（badly affected）”，这吻合选项D的“受到负面影响”。
你可能会根据大象体型大的常识觉得它们不怕蜜蜂，导致你忽略了整体听音，但录音特意点出了小象这个弱势群体会受到严重伤害。

Yes, and then there are the baby elephants, the calves, which have thinner skin, so they can be really badly affected, especially if they get attacked by a whole swarm of bees. So elephants with babies may be threatened by bees even if they don't get stung themselves.

questions.question: How did the elephants respond to the audio recording of bees?

analyses.content: 录音生动描述了大象听到声音后，朝着反方向“狂奔（dashed off）”并且“不停回头看（kept turning their heads around）”，完全契合选项B。
听到“停下（stopped）”时你可能会着急选C，但大象停下并非为了“寻找声音来源”，它们随后的动作是迅速逃跑，很容易因为抓错动作细节而掉进陷阱。

Well, they've got a recording of a swarm of angry bees, and they played it to herds of elephants out in the wild, and they all stopped what they were doing immediately and stood erect with their heads up and their ears extended. They must have been really aware there was danger somewhere. But not the sort of danger that they can face up to and charge. So they dashed off in the opposite direction. They kept turning their heads around.

questions.question: The reason why one herd of elephants didn't run away

analyses.content: 录音里给出了明确的结论，指出这群大象没跑是因为它们完全“缺乏任何关于蜜蜂的经验（lacked any experience of bees）”，对应选项B。
一开始听到“没听清（didn't hear it properly）”你可能顺手就选了A，但那只是初步猜测，录音紧跟着用“实际上得出的结论（actually concluded）”给出了真正的原因。

Maybe that herd just didn't hear it properly. It seems a very small exception to the main finding. I think researchers actually concluded that this particular herd lacked any experience of bees. They've never encountered any, so they weren't afraid of the recording.

questions.question: What surprised the researchers when elephants heard the recording?

analyses.content: 录音中提到让研究人员惊讶的点在于，有一半的大象在听到声音后的“10秒内就非常迅速地（very quickly within ten seconds）”做出了反应，对应选项A的“立即反应”。
你非常容易被“10秒（ten seconds）”这个数字干扰而错选B，但录音的意思是在极短的反应时间内作出了反击行动，而不是“仅仅害怕了10秒”。

Exactly. But what surprised the researchers was from the seventeen herds they did take action when they heard the recording, they found almost fifty percent of the herds did this very quickly within ten seconds of hearing the recording.

questions.question: What is the drawback of the application of bee recording?

analyses.content: 录音指出这个设备的难点在于，必须得有人去把它布置好并且确保它能运转，是个实打实的“活儿（job）”，这与选项B中“培训人去布置设备”吻合。
你可能听到电或者电池就去考虑A或C，但录音里明确表示电力其实并不难解决（用电池就可以），真正的难点是需要人工去设置，没跟上整体语意就会选错。

You've got to have the electricity to run the machinery. No, that's okay. It can run on batteries, but the whole thing's quite difficult for electrical outlet, which might be easy, and then someone's got to set it all out and make sure it's working. That's not difficult, but it's really a job.

questions.question: What is the other effective method as a deterrent to elephants?

analyses.content: 录音明确提到，当人们把牛铃（cowbells）挂在栅栏上时，似乎就能把大象吓跑，直接锁定了选项A。
你肯定听到了电网（electric fences）和辣椒（chili peppers）这两个干扰项，但录音无情地说电网“没多大成功”，辣椒也“根本没吓住大象”，没听完后面的排除评价就选极容易中招。

They're trying other methods as well, like electric fences to keep the elephants away from the crops. They haven't had much success. But when they hang cowbells on the fences, that seemed to scare them off. Yes. I've read they tried chili peppers as a deterrent too, but that didn't scare the elephants at all.
